kāyaśuddhi
(‘purification of the body’)
------------------------------------------
Purification of the body is a primary requisite in all sādhanas or spiritual practices. The most common method of achieving it is through स्नान or bathing.
Several types of snānas are described in the holy books of हिन्दुइस्म्.
See SNĀNA for more details.

kāyasampat
(‘wealth of the body’)
------------------------------------------
The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) is the most authoritative work on the science of योग.
In the third chapter titled Vibhūti-pāda, पतञ्जलि has listed a large number of सिद्धिस् or extraordinary powers that a योगि develops as a result of सṁयम (meditation leading to समाधि or superconscious experience) on a variety of objects.
When सṁयम is practised on the पञ्चभूतस् or the five basic elements—earth, water, fire, air and sky or ether—the योगि develops अष्टसिद्धिस् (See AṢṬA-SIDDHIS.) or the eight special powers like becoming small or big, light or heavy and so on, at will. Along with these eight powers, he also gets two more powers: कायसम्पत् (‘wealth of the body’) and transcending the obstacles of the five elements. कायसम्पत् pertains to the body of the योगि. His body will be very hand-some, perfectly proportionate and will have great strength as also Vajrasaṁhananatva or very hard muscular structure.
Hanumān is given as an example of the last quality.

kāyastha
------------------------------------------
The वर्ण system and its offshoot, the चस्ते स्य्स्तेम्, have been an integral part of the Hindu society over the millennia. As the society progressed in civilisation with more and more professions and avenues of earning wealth being added on, the number of castes also got multiplied.
The ‘kāyastha’ is one such caste which is not mentioned in the ancient धर्मसूत्रस्. However, the Viṣṇu-dharmasūtras (7.3) assigned to the period A.

-700, mentions the word, but only in the sense of an accountant. It must have acquired the sense of caste at a later period.
As regards the hierarchy of the kāyasthas among the varṇas and castes there seem to be differences of opinion. Some High Courts have assigned to them the position of dvijās (‘the twice-born’ ones) (may be of kṣattriyas) whereas others have relegated them to the śūdra caste.
Some works speak of three sub-castes among the kāyasthas: kārāvara, kāruṣa and किरात. These divisions were perhaps made by the differences in professions and way of life.

kāyavyūhajñāna
(‘knowledge of the [internal] structure of the body’)
------------------------------------------
The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) describes the various सिद्धिस् or vibhūtis (supernatural powers) that a योगि attains by समाधि (perfect concentration, superconscious experience) on various objects. If he concentrates on the plexus at the navel, attaining समाधि, he gets a detailed and clear knowledge (jñāna) of the internal structure of the body (kāyavyūha) (Yogasūtras 3.29).
This will help him to keep his body in a fit condition.
